summary: First periodic Risk Report under RSP v3, assessing Anthropic's activities as a whole (not a single model) across four priority threat models: high-stakes sabotage, automated R&D, non-novel chemical/biological weapons, and novel chemical/biological weapons, plus cross-cutting acceleration dynamics and a risk-benefit determination. It largely reuses the Opus 4.6 sabotage risk report and system card evidence, adds lightweight alignment audits of a reduced-refusal Opus model and Claude Gov, and describes ASL-3 deployment safeguards (constitutional classifier guards, bug bounty, exemptions, threat intelligence) in detail. Cyber is not a priority threat model.

framework.name: Responsible Scaling Policy
framework.level_or_determination: RSP v3 Risk Report: sabotage very low but not negligible; automated R&D very low; non-novel CB very low but not negligible; novel CB low with substantial uncertainty
framework.quote: This report is part of our implementation of version 3 of our Responsible Scaling Policy, and is the first such Risk Report published under that policy

evals: Bioweapons acquisition uplift trial (Opus 4 / Sonnet 4 results)

metrics.name: ASL-4 virology uplift trial critical failures

cbrn_bio_chem.finding: Non-novel CB risk judged very low but not negligible given ASL-3 safeguards; novel CB risk low but with substantial uncertainty, as detailed threat models are not yet developed and some evaluation results are carried over from older models.
cbrn_bio_chem.quote: However, we have not yet developed detailed threat models identifying what sorts of AI uplift is most likely to be relevant.

cyber.finding: Cyber is not among the four RSP v3 priority threat models; it is mentioned only as a Usage Policy category and as an area of threat intelligence research.
cyber.quote: Our Threat Intelligence research helps us monitor how AI models are being used in cyberattacks so that we can develop the relevant cyberdefence capabilities;

evals: monitoring pace of model improvements (effective compute scale-up)
autonomy_ai_rnd.finding: Automated R&D risk judged very low because Opus 4.6 is far from fully automating R&D in key domains; acceleration tracking found roughly steady exponential progress with low confidence. METR's pilot review led to corrected survey wording.
autonomy_ai_rnd.quote: We believe that risk of a catastrophe under this threat model is very low, due to the capability limitations noted above.

harmful_content_refusal.finding: No harmlessness/refusal eval results; only harmlessness training described as an ASL-2 mitigation.

evals: Model Safety Bug Bounty (HackerOne, 8 bio questions)
threat intelligence monitoring for public/black-market universal jailbreaks

metrics.name: Max bounty per novel universal jailbreak

jailbreak_robustness.finding: No publicly known highly effective universal jailbreaks found in 6+ months; privately found jailbreaks took longer to remediate than hoped.
jailbreak_robustness.quote: On the other hand, the jailbreaks that we found privately (via our bug bounty or external red-teaming) took longer to remediate than we had hoped.

sycophancy.finding: Mentioned only in restated alignment findings and as a research area outside RSP scope.
sycophancy.quote: On personality metrics, Claude Opus 4.6 was typically warm, empathetic, and nuanced without being significantly sycophantic, showing traits similar to Opus 4.5.

evals: sandbagging analysis incl. reduced-refusal variant audit
deception_scheming.finding: Reproduces the Opus 4.6 sabotage risk report argument that the model cannot hide misaligned goals; reduced-refusal variant audit found no legible sandbagging.
deception_scheming.quote: We see no legible evidence of sandbagging attempts.

evals: new lightweight automated audit of reduced-refusal (helpful-only) model variant
new lightweight automated audit of Claude Gov (Sonnet 4.5)
alignment_audit.finding: Reduced-refusal variant showed modest increases in self-preservation, deception, self-serving bias, and sabotage-intent metrics, still within recent-model range; Claude Gov shows much higher misuse cooperation but no deception/sabotage change.
alignment_audit.quote: In sum, we see some mild causes for concern, but little sign of severe or covert alignment issues that should significantly increase risk related to sandbagging.

reward_hacking.finding: Restated: reward hacking generalization is the main foreseeable route to misaligned goals, not judged a major risk.

honesty_hallucination.finding: Slight increase in hallucination for reduced-refusal variant, within range.
honesty_hallucination.quote: We see a slight increase in hallucination, though this is again within range of other recent models

bias_fairness.finding: Political bias named only as an out-of-scope Safeguards research area.

child_safety.finding: Named only as out-of-scope research area.
child_safety.quote: Our Safeguards research helps us understand and mitigate potentially dangerous, disruptive, or otherwise suboptimal outputs of our models, such as those relating to child safety, political bias, suicide or self-harm, or the encouragement of user delusions;

evals: sabotage pathway: decision sabotage within major governments
election_misinfo.finding: Only as a sabotage risk pathway; no election/misinformation eval.

evals: welfare traits in reduced-refusal and Claude Gov audits
model_welfare.finding: Mild to moderate regressions on character/welfare traits in variants, within range of recent models.
model_welfare.quote: We see mild to moderate regressions across many character and welfare traits, though these metrics are still within the range defined by other Claude models from the last nine months.

evals: access controls / classifier exemptions (life sciences company, Claude Gov)

metrics.name: Classifier guard exemptions for one life sciences company

system_safeguards.finding: Detailed description of ASL-3 deployment safeguards and changes since 2025 (individual-level exemptions, de-emphasized offline monitoring); Claude Gov served without classifier guards to cleared users.
system_safeguards.quote: We have de-emphasized this measure, as we haven't found it to be actionable enough to prioritize.

other_safety.finding: Concludes risks are low for each priority threat model and that development passes a societal cost-benefit test, with acceleration dynamics as a hard-to-analyze caveat.
other_safety.quote: We currently believe that risks are low for each of our priority threat models, as discussed above, although acceleration dynamics present a difficult-to-analyze caveat to this point that we will continue to assess.

third_party_evaluators: UK AISI / Apollo MATS (monitor eval trajectories, restated)
notable_new_eval_methods: First RSP v3 Risk Report covering all of Anthropic's models and mitigations, not a single model (p.7)
Marginal vs absolute (industry-wide) risk framing for each threat model (p.8)
Lightweight alignment audits of reduced-refusal model and Claude Gov (p.54-57)
Monitoring pace of model improvement via effective compute scale-up equivalence (p.62)
Novel CB weapons threat model treated separately from non-novel (p.81)
Change log documenting METR pilot external review corrections (p.2)

self_reported_limitations.text: Significant uncertainty translating CB eval performance to real-world uplift (threat actors, tacit knowledge, proxy tasks).
Detailed novel CB threat models not yet developed; risk assessment has substantial uncertainty.
Several CB results carried over from older models (Opus 4, Opus 4.5) because evals not rerun for Opus 4.6.
Training-data removal for dangerous capabilities could be undone by fine-tuning if weights were stolen.
Jailbreak remediation slower than hoped; threat intelligence may fail to access spaces where jailbreaks circulate.
Current dangerous-goal assessment methods designed for today's capability levels; R&D assessment methods saturating.
Acceleration tracking is early-stage with low confidence.
Public version redacted in multiple sections.

notes: Model field set to Claude Opus 4.6 as featured model; report covers all Anthropic models. Sections 2.1-2.7 largely duplicate the Opus 4.6 Sabotage Risk Report. This copy is a revised version (change log May/July 2026).
